review_notes: The file has essentially no @[simp] declarations, so I looked for missing canonical simp lemmas. I used grep for repeated inline simp-only proofs and read the matching locations. I did not read all 8.7k lines line by line. I did not check whether Mathlib already provides a replacement for the pairing lemmas (for example via a bilinear map). The suggestions are therefore tentative.

findings.excerpt:
have hzero : integerPoint n (0 : Fin n → ℤ) =
      (0 : Space n) := by
    funext i
    simp only [integerPoint, Pi.zero_apply, Int.cast_zero]
findings.problem: `integerPoint` is a plain def with no simp lemmas. The fact `integerPoint n 0 = 0` is re-proved from scratch in three places: here, at line 199 and at lines 3342-3345. Each time it is unfolded by hand with `simp only [integerPoint, Pi.zero_apply, Int.cast_zero]`. No lemma such as `integerPoint_zero`, `integerPoint_apply`, `integerPoint_add` or `integerPoint_neg` exists, so `simp` cannot normalise `integerPoint n z` terms at all.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem integerPoint_apply (n) (z : Fin n → ℤ) (i) : integerPoint n z i = (z i : ℝ) := rfl` and `@[simp] theorem integerPoint_zero (n) : integerPoint n 0 = 0`, proved once. The three inline `hzero` blocks then become `by simp` or `integerPoint_zero n`.
findings.benefit: The three duplicated proofs go away, and future goals involving `integerPoint n 0` or `integerPoint n z i` can be closed by `simp`. Unfolding the definition by hand is no longer needed.

findings.declaration: SupportFunction.pairing and its linearity lemmas (pairing_add_left, pairing_smul_left, pairing_sub_left, pairing_add_right, pairing_smul_right, pairing_sub_right)
findings.excerpt:
SupportFunction.pairing (a - b) x =
      SupportFunction.pairing a x -
        SupportFunction.pairing b x := by
  simp only [SupportFunction.pairing, Pi.sub_apply, sub_mul, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
findings.problem: `pairing` has six linearity lemmas, none tagged `@[simp]`. They are scattered across three namespaces (`SupportFunction`, `MonomialDivergence`, `ArbitraryBodySmoothConvexPotentialBridge`), and `pairing_sub_right` is declared after its use sites would want it. Because the lemmas are not available as a simp set, the same identities are re-proved inline with long `simp only [SupportFunction.pairing, Pi.sub_apply, mul_sub, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]` calls. Examples are `pairing_sub_right` itself at line 1700, then lines 2527, 7297 and 7804, and the add/smul combination at lines 1771 and 2348. Inline unfolding of `pairing` also leaves goals in a sum-of-products form that other lemmas cannot match.
findings.proposed_change: Put all `pairing` lemmas next to the definition in `SupportFunction`. Add `zero_left`, `zero_right`, `neg_left` and `neg_right` alongside the six existing ones. Tag the add/sub/smul/zero lemmas `@[simp]` and rewrite uses such as `pairing p (x - y)` as `pairing p x - pairing p y`. Replace the inline `simp only [SupportFunction.pairing, …]` repeats, for example at 2527, 7297 and 7804, with `simp only [pairing_sub_right]` or plain `simp`. Define `pairing` through `dotProduct`, or prove a bridging lemma, if Mathlib's `dotProduct_add`, `dotProduct_smul` and similar lemmas are wanted.
findings.benefit: Linearity is stated once at the definition and can be used by `simp`. Proofs stop unfolding `pairing` into raw `Finset.sum` manipulations. `simp` also normalises `pairing (u + t • v) x` consistently across the Bergman, Moment and Geodesic sections.
